title: Armed Federal Agents Knock on Doors in Multi-State Noncitizen Voter Inquiry
meta_title: Armed DHS Agents Knock on Doors in Noncitizen Voter Sweep
meta_description: Federal agents are questioning residents about voter status in several states ahead of the midterms, sparking lawsuits and voter intimidation concerns.
discover_titles: DHS Deploys Armed Agents to Knock on Doors Over Noncitizen Voting
Armed Federal Agents Question Residents on Voting History Ahead of Midterms
Federal Door-Knocking Operation Targeting Noncitizen Voters Sparks Backlash
spot: Armed Department of Homeland Security agents have begun visiting homes across multiple states ahead of the midterm elections to interrogate residents about their immigration and voter registration status, triggering legal challenges over potential voter intimidation.
content_html:
Key Developments

Uniformed and armed agents from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) have been knocking on doors in several states to question residents about their citizenship and determine whether they have registered or cast ballots in previous elections, according to a CBS News investigation. The visits, which ramped up significantly in September during the height of the midterm campaign season, continued into mid-October.

As part of the broader enforcement effort, the Department of Justice announced that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents arrested more than 20 green card holders in California on charges of unlawfully registering or voting. In one operation, dozens of federal agents descended upon the home of a 72-year-old Belizean national, arresting him in his pajamas under allegations that he illegally voted across four consecutive election cycles.

A DHS spokesperson defended the actions, stating that HSI is focused on rooting out election fraud under President Trump to ensure only American citizens participate in elections. However, former HSI agent Eric Balliet noted that such door-to-door voting inquiries represent an unprecedented departure from standard federal law enforcement practices during his 23-year career.

Key Takeaways

  • Federal Field Inquiries: Armed DHS personnel are actively conducting residential visits to question individuals about their citizenship and voting participation.
  • California Arrests: More than 20 legal permanent residents have been taken into custody by federal authorities over allegations of unlawful voting activity.
  • Disputed Claims: While DHS claims as many as 250,000 noncitizens could be registered illegally, Justice Department records show only 156 individuals have faced voter-fraud charges out of 227 million registered U.S. voters.

Why It Matters

The aggressive door-knocking campaign has drawn sharp condemnation from voting rights advocates, leading the legal group Protect Democracy to file a lawsuit against the federal agency. Critics argue that sending armed federal agents to private residences bypasses state-level voter roll verification procedures and creates an intimidating atmosphere that could suppress participation among lawful, naturalized voters just weeks before casting ballots.
